title: Check the Ego
coreMove: notice when status protection is blocking help, correction, or cooperation, and put the mission back above looking right
sourcePressure: Elite-unit arrogance damages coordination, while humility and cross-unit respect return attention to the mission.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter

counterintuition: leadership is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: ask yourself how to be a better leader

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

exampleSpecs.domain: aircraft maintenance bay where an apprentice catches a senior tech’s missed cotter pin
exampleSpecs.audience: a lead mechanic known for being the best in the hangar
exampleSpecs.stakes: status pride can turn a real safety catch into silence next time
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead mechanic repeats the apprentice’s concern aloud, checks the assembly in front of the crew, and thanks him before touching the tool cart
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bent cotter pin sits half-seated under the landing-gear light

exampleSpecs.domain: surgical suite where a scrub nurse challenges the attending’s count
exampleSpecs.audience: a senior surgeon under schedule pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: ego can push past a safety stop that exists for a reason
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the surgeon feels the room waiting, lowers the instrument, asks for the count again, and treats the pause as protecting the patient rather than challenging his authority
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are close enough to see this: blue sponge-count board shows one blank square beside the OR clock.

exampleSpecs.domain: fine-dining kitchen corrected by a health inspector
exampleSpecs.audience: a chef-owner whose reputation is built on precision
exampleSpecs.stakes: defensiveness can keep a temperature problem alive after the inspector leaves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chef stops arguing about his record, checks the inspector’s probe reading against his own log, and changes the holding process before dinner service
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The first thing you register is physical: probe thermometer rests in a pan of duck confit reading four degrees too warm.

exampleSpecs.domain: elite cycling training camp where support staff flags a brake issue
exampleSpecs.audience: a team captain who dismisses slower riders and mechanics
exampleSpecs.stakes: status rivalry can turn a preventable crash into a team failure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain hands the bike to the mechanic, asks the support rider what she felt on descent, and makes the squad inspect brakes before the next climb
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Hold there," someone says. Carbon brake pad leaves a gray smear across a mechanic’s glove.

exampleSpecs.domain: venture-backed startup founder reading support tickets after a botched release
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder convinced customers just resist change
exampleSpecs.stakes: ego can convert useful feedback into noise while churn accelerates
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the founder reads three refund transcripts out loud, removes his defensive wording from the release note, and asks support to mark the confusing step in the product
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Later, the team will trace the lesson back to this: refund transcript prints with the same sentence highlighted three times.

exampleSpecs.domain: bridge repair review where a welder spots a crack the engineer missed
exampleSpecs.audience: a licensed engineer overseeing an overnight lane closure
exampleSpecs.stakes: credential pride can bury field knowledge that protects the structure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the engineer kneels beside the welder, looks at the dye mark, revises the repair sequence, and names the welder’s catch in the shift briefing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What changes once this is in front of everyone: red dye bleeds from a hairline crack under a portable work light?

skillTargets: distinguish confidence from ego in a concrete decision
choose the mission-first response to correction or outside help

tryThisNowSpec: Find one correction you disliked this week and write the mission value inside it before you defend yourself.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
